title: Linking through unique identifier during registration
description: Homeowner's personal data is linked to their identity through unique identifiers collected during account registration, enabling cross-referencing of data across systems.

title: Processing of identified data during registration
description: Homeowner's identifiable information (name, contact details, etc.) is requested and processed during account registration.

title: Unique identifier in registration data
description: Registration data contains unique references to the homeowner's identity that can be used to identify the data subject.

title: Attributable data evidence from registration
description: Registration records can be attributed to the homeowner, preventing them from denying certain claims about their account or data usage.

title: Data type sensitivity in registration
description: Registration may collect more sensitive personal data types than functionally required for basic account creation.

title: Excessive volume of personal data
description: Registration may process more personal data than functionally needed for the account creation process.

title: Unawareness of data processing
description: Homeowner may not be fully aware of how their personal data will be collected, processed, stored, or disclosed during registration.

title: Lack of control over data processing preferences
description: Homeowner may lack control to set preferences or consent in how their personal data is processed during registration.

title: Insufficient data subject controls
description: Registration process may lack adequate support for data subject rights such as access, rectification, or erasure.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Registration may process more personal data than is actually needed for the functional goals of the system.

title: Unnecessary data treatment
description: Motion/door/sensor events may be further treated, analyzed, or enriched in ways not strictly necessary for the functional goal of logging events.
assumptions: Assumes the Home Hub may perform additional processing on the raw sensor data beyond simple storage.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain without knowing the exact processing performed by the Home Hub on the sensor events.

title: Excessive volume of data
description: The volume of motion/door/sensor events stored may exceed what is functionally needed for the system's purpose.
assumptions: Assumes continuous or frequent logging of all sensor events.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain without knowing the logging frequency and retention policy.

title: Identifier in sensor data
description: Sensor events may contain unique identifiers (timestamps, locations, device IDs) that can be used to identify individuals.
assumptions: Assumes sensor events include identifying attributes.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain without knowing the exact attributes captured in the sensor events.

title: Attributable data evidence
description: Stored sensor events can be used to attribute specific actions or events to individuals.
assumptions: Assumes events can be linked to specific individuals through timestamps or other attributes.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain without knowing how events are linked to individuals.

title: Excessive video data collection
description: Camera clips may contain more video data than functionally required for the upload purpose, potentially including unnecessary metadata or full-resolution footage.

title: Excessive volume of personal data
description: The volume of camera clips being uploaded may exceed what is functionally needed for the intended purpose of video storage.

title: Data propagation to cloud services
description: Camera clips are propagated to cloud storage services where they may be accessible by parties beyond the intended functional scope.

title: Extended data retention
description: Camera clips may be retained in cloud storage longer than functionally needed for the intended purpose.

title: Identifiable information in video clips
description: Camera clips may contain unique identifiers such as faces, license plates, or other personally identifiable information.

title: Revealing attributes in video data
description: Video data may include revealing attributes that support identification of data subjects within the recorded footage.

title: Unawareness of data processing
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their camera footage is being collected, processed, and stored in cloud services.

title: Lack of data subject control
description: Data subjects may lack control over how their camera footage is processed, stored, and shared in the cloud system.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing of camera clips may violate GDPR data minimization principle if more personal data is processed than actually needed.

title: Potential unlawful processing
description: Processing of camera footage may not be lawful if consent is not obtained or lawful basis is unclear.

title: Data shared with external analytics vendor
description: Device-usage analytics are shared with an external cloud analytics vendor (EE3), which may exceed the functional necessity of the mobile app backend's purpose.
assumptions: The analytics vendor is a predetermined, known party, but the data may be more broadly accessible than needed.

title: Potentially sensitive data types disclosed
description: Device-usage analytics may include sensitive information about user behavior patterns that could be perceived as highly sensitive, even if aggregated.
assumptions: Device-usage data can reveal sensitive patterns about user habits, preferences, or activities.

title: Quasi-identifier data in aggregated analytics
description: Aggregated device-usage analytics may contain combinations of attributes that could serve as quasi-identifiers, potentially allowing re-identification of individuals.
assumptions: Aggregation does not guarantee complete anonymization; quasi-identifiers may still exist in the data.

title: Data subject unawareness of analytics sharing
description: Users may not be aware that their device-usage analytics are being shared with external analytics vendors.
assumptions: Users may not have explicit knowledge or consent for this specific data sharing activity.

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Device-usage analytics may be processed beyond what is functionally needed for the mobile app's core functionality.
assumptions: The analytics sharing may not be strictly necessary for the app's primary purpose.

title: Sensitive video content may be unnecessarily disclosed
description: The stored video clip may contain sensitive personal data (e.g., home surveillance footage, private moments) that is being retrieved and made accessible to the mobile app backend. If the video contains sensitive data, its retrieval and processing may exceed what is functionally required for playback.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain without knowing the specific content of the video clip being stored.
